messages.content: Our gateway is drowning in reconnects after every deploy. Clients reconnect instantly and hammer the handshake endpoint.

content.text: That is a reconnect storm: on disconnect every client retries immediately. Add exponential backoff with jitter on the client, and have the server send a Retry-After hint in the close frame during deploys. Jitter matters more than the backoff curve - without it all clients retry in lockstep.

Full jitter: delay = random(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt)). It spreads retries across the whole window and is the standard formulation (AWS architecture blog). Cap at 30s so a healthy server is re-found quickly.

messages.content: We need per-API-key rate limiting for the public endpoints. Sliding window or token bucket?

content.text: Token bucket. It allows short bursts (which real clients produce) while capping the sustained rate, and it is O(1) per request: refill lazily from the elapsed time, decrement on use. Sliding window counters are cheaper but punish bursty-but-legitimate clients.

Redis with a small Lua script so the read-refill-write is atomic. Store per key: token count and last-refill timestamp. Set the bucket capacity to the burst you want to tolerate and the refill rate to the sustained limit.

title: Migrate test suite from Jest to Vitest

messages.content: Thinking of moving the test suite from Jest to Vitest. What breaks?

content.text: Three recurring breakages: jest.mock hoisting semantics differ (vi.mock is eager by default), snapshot format changes, and setup files move from jest.config setupFiles to vitest config. Everything else - describe/it/expect - is API-compatible.

For a Vite-based app, yes: shared transform pipeline means the tests and the build agree on module semantics, and watch mode is dramatically faster. For a webpack app the migration cost usually outweighs the benefit.
